import z3

# Social Golfers: 50 golfers, 10 groups of 5, 6 weeks
# No pair of golfers in same group more than once

NUM_GOLFERS = 50
NUM_GROUPS = 10
GROUP_SIZE = 5
NUM_WEEKS = 6

# Create solver
solver = z3.Solver()

# Decision variables: x[w][g][p] = 1 if golfer p is in group g in week w
# We'll use a simpler encoding: for each week w and golfer p, which group they're in
# group[w][p] is an integer 0..9

group = [[z3.Int(f"group_{w}_{p}") for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS)] for w in range(NUM_WEEKS)]

# Domain constraints: each group assignment is 0..9
for w in range(NUM_WEEKS):
    for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS):
        solver.add(z3.And(group[w][p] >= 0, group[w][p] < NUM_GROUPS))

# Each group in each week has exactly GROUP_SIZE golfers
for w in range(NUM_WEEKS):
    for g in range(NUM_GROUPS):
        # Count golfers in this group
        count = z3.Sum([z3.If(group[w][p] == g, 1, 0) for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS)])
        solver.add(count == GROUP_SIZE)

# No pair of golfers in same group more than once
# For each pair (p1, p2) with p1 < p2, at most one week where they're in the same group
for p1 in range(NUM_GOLFERS):
    for p2 in range(p1 + 1, NUM_GOLFERS):
        same_group_weeks = [z3.If(group[w][p1] == group[w][p2], 1, 0) for w in range(NUM_WEEKS)]
        solver.add(z3.Sum(same_group_weeks) <= 1)

print(f"Variables: {NUM_WEEKS * NUM_GOLFERS}")
print(f"Constraints created, starting solver...")
print("This may take a while...")

# Set a timeout
